propositions: Operators resort to --force to close 25+ non-bug tickets (task/story/epic) with administrative dispositions (duplicate/obsolete/superseded/wontfix) because the completion-verification gate has no truthful exit for non-completion closes and the available disposition path is scoped to bugs only.
The close-precheck refusal message never mentions the narrow attested-disposition path that does exist, leaving operators unaware of administrative-class alternatives to --force.

Non-bug tickets cannot close with disposition classes not_a_bug or escalated (bug-only vocabulary); administrative closes on non-bugs require a restricted set {duplicate, obsolete, superseded, wontfix} enforced at the write-side gate.

obsolete and wontfix dispositions require a supplied reason; the reason persists as a distinct close_reason key on the close event (separate from force_close_reason) and must appear in signed disposition attestations.

A reason-only administrative close (obsolete/wontfix without a replacement link) skips completion verification and routes directly to disposition verdict; replacement-bearing classes (duplicate/superseded) demand a live replacement link via _ensure_duplicate_close_is_linked.
The close-precheck FAIL message enumerates applicable --class values for the ticket's type, enabling discovery of the truthful administrative-disposition exit without --force.
